title: Week 2 Overview: From Promises to Labeled Pixels
text: Last week the boxes were a promise. This week the promise closed. This is sigh. Every image that passed quality control last week is now annotated. About 136 of them, one class common loon. Every box drawn by hand. That set is ready for the latest yolo. And 136 is a small number. It is supposed to be because each one had to get past the check before it was allowed to count. Here is what is actually in it. Frames pulled off the web. Frames shot from shore on a Nikon. Frames flown over open water by drone. One class label across all of them. title: Inside the Dataset: Pulling Frames from Web, Shore, and Drones
text: Annotated. Nothing was labeled that was going to be thrown away. And this is the set. Read back the way the trainer sees it. Every box drawn by hand. One label on all of them. Common loon. Now look at the range. In some frames, the bird fills half the picture. In others, the box is smaller than its own caption. A dark smudge a few pixels across on open water. Same label. The same model has to find both. That is not one detection problem. It is two wearing one name. Close in, the bird is unmistakable. The collar, the beak, the red eye, hundreds of pixels of evidence. title: The Core Challenge: Distinguishing Large Birds from Tiny Smudges
text: Frames will make this model look good early. The far ones are where it actually gets judged. So, train now or keep annotating. 136 frames is a small set, and the pull is to wait until it is big enough to win on. But the first run is not a test of the detector. It is a test of the plumbing that the labels parse the classes map the loss moves. Better to know that before there are a thousand more boxes to redo. So week two every quality checked image annotated by hand about 136 of them one class ready for the latest yolo. Nothing trained yet. The set is small and it is clean and small and clean is the only version of this you can still fix cheaply. Your

title: Testing the Plumbing: Why You Should Train Small and Clean First
text: Turn. If you have a labeled set sitting ready, do not train it yet. Open the label file and sort every box by area. Look at the smallest tenth and the largest. If those two groups do not look like the same problem, you do not have one data set. You have two. And one average score is going to hide whichever of them is failing. Every box checked. Next week, the first yolo run. Sigh.
